meta.description: Character LoRA on IllustriousXL (SDXL arch) for a 16GB laptop GPU. Recipe values (rank 32/alpha 32 + conv 16/16, adamw8bit, LR 1e-4, 1024 training resolution) are UNCHANGED from illxl_char_lora. The point of this variant is batch discipline: this preset keeps batch 1 and reaches an effective batch of 2 via gradient_accumulation 2, trading wall-clock for VRAM. Effective batch 2, not 4: the step suggestion divides by effective batch, and at 4 that quotient drops under the arch's step floor on any small/medium dataset, gets clamped back up, and silently inflates real per-image exposure 2-3x past target - the advisor then recommends a step count its own exposure gauge would flag as fry-risk. The advisor's Illustrious recipe now also recommends batch 2, so the two agree; it remains VRAM-unaware, so on this machine reach effective batch through accumulation as configured here rather than raising batch size. Note the advisor also suggests a HIGHER LR for Illustrious (2e-4 small / 3e-4 otherwise) than the 1e-4 inherited here, and its optimizer choice is genuinely contested in the source guides (adamw8bit + constant vs Prodigy + cosine) - those are recipe questions, unaffected by this hardware profile, and are left exactly as the parent preset had them. Other deltas: low_vram true, cache_latents true alongside cache_latents_to_disk so latents are served from RAM rather than re-read and deep-copied from disk every step (native Windows runs the dataloader at num_workers 0), and ui_db_poll_seconds 2 to throttle the UI's per-step sqlite polling (cost: up to 2s of latency on the stop/save-now buttons). Left unquantized like the parent, holding quantization in reserve as an OOM lever. NOT measured on 16GB hardware. Point model.name_or_path at your local Illustrious checkpoint if you have one. Use booru-style tag captions with a unique trigger tag first. If you swap the optimizer to an Automagic variant, this batch-1-plus-accumulation pattern will not work as-is - Automagic fuses its step into the backward pass by default, so gradient_accumulation must go back to 1 and the effective batch reached by raising batch size instead. Speed (2026-08-29): latents are served from RAM after the first pass (cache_latents + cache_latents_to_disk — disk-only caching re-read every latent every step), loss_sync_every 4, ui_db_poll_seconds 2. Training math unchanged. STEP TABLE (meta.step_table, 2026-10-12, machine-independent - the same table ships on every IllustriousXL/SDXL preset, laptop or desktop): 20 images ~1750, 30 images ~2500, 50 images ~3000, exact-count interpolation between rows, capped at 3000 steps. OPTIMIZED DATASET COUNT ~50 images: that is where the cap is reached; past it the panel keeps 3000 and the exposure gauge says the dataset is past the optimal size for this model and suggests curating down, instead of calling it undertrained. Source: community Illustrious/SDXL character guides: 15-20 images 1500-2000 steps, 20-30 images 2000-3000 (sanj.dev, r/StableDiffusion primer 2026-01), Illustrious converging around 3000 (SeaArt guide; night-dev ai-toolkit guide starts at 3000; note.com 30 images x 10 repeats x 10 epochs = 3000). Values are steps at effective batch 1; the Step Suggestion panel divides by your effective batch (batch_size x gradient_accumulation), which is the only thing that differs between machines. Below the first row the first row's steps apply.
